## AI-generated surface maps (2026-10-19)

Generated with the built-in ImageGen tool, not the API/CLI. These are original artistic surface maps, not NASA observations or live weather. The original files are retained in the project's assets directory. Each generated image is 1774 × 887 pixels; no synthetic resolution increase is applied.

- `earth-cloud-density-v1.png`: grayscale cloud opacity, sampled on a separate elevated sphere with cloud shadows.
- `gas-giant-albedo-v1.png`: diffuse atmosphere surface, lit and shaded in 3D; the ring geometry is generated by the renderer.
- `../ai-universe-lettering-bold.json`: bold lettering outlines derived from the local Arial Bold font for extruded geometry. No font binary is distributed.

The user's two YouTube links were viewed only as motion and lighting references; their video or audio is not embedded or downloaded:
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ntu7WaBYYy4 — low-orbit clouds, dark ocean, thin atmospheric limb.
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CVmuzJq0u20 — fine stars and forward depth motion.

### Final prompt: Earth cloud density

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production PBR cloud opacity texture for a realistic 3D Earth sphere in a premium corporate anniversary space film. Generate ONE highly detailed seamless 2:1 equirectangular global cloud density map, 4096x2048 if possible. This is a flat UV texture, NOT a globe render and NOT a view from orbit. Pure black background for clear atmosphere, white and soft neutral gray for layered volumetric clouds only. Scientifically plausible Earth weather: finely textured broken cumulus fields, thin cirrus filaments, a few curling midlatitude frontal bands, one subtle spiral storm, large open clear regions. 45 percent global cloud coverage, rich micro detail, wispy soft edges, avoid thick solid white blocks. Even unlit diffuse density, no shadows, no lighting, no atmosphere glow, no stars, no ocean, no land, no text, no labels, no grid. Left and right edges must join seamlessly, natural polar mapping. Photorealistic NASA orbital cloud structure, understated and natural. Output only the grayscale equirectangular texture.

### Final prompt: Gas giant albedo

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production PBR albedo texture for a physically shaded 3D gas giant passing a camera in a refined cinematic universe animation. Generate ONE extremely detailed seamless 2:1 equirectangular gas-giant surface color map, 4096x2048 if possible. Flat UV map, NOT a sphere render. Entire canvas filled with realistic fine atmospheric bands and subtle turbulent eddies; slate blue, dusty ivory, muted warm gray, deep desaturated navy. Analogous in realism to Saturn and Neptune, elegant restrained colors, very fine layered cloud turbulence instead of broad cartoon stripes, one small coherent oval storm. Uniform diffuse light across the texture, no baked highlights, no terminator, no lighting gradient, no stars, no rings, no black margins, no text. Left and right edges join seamlessly. Photorealistic detailed satellite atmospheric surface texture with natural irregularity.

### Final prompt: cinematic orbital Earth

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: final premium cinematic Earth orbital matte painting with genuine alpha for a 3D corporate anniversary animation. Wide 2:1 composition, highest native detail. Photorealistic low Earth orbit photography looking across the curved limb over the Pacific ocean at dawn, like a real astronaut camera rather than a computer globe. Earth fills the lower 60 percent and extends beyond left, right and bottom edges; the curved horizon apex is at x60%, y40% of the image, dropping gently towards the two sides. All outer space ABOVE the Earth and its very thin atmosphere must be genuinely transparent alpha. The Earth is not a complete circular planet: close low-orbit arc only. Deep ink blue ocean, finely resolved bright stratocumulus fields and translucent cirrus with real layered cloud shadows, one graceful broken frontal cloud band, cloud structures in the middle distance sharply resolved, realistic gradual aerial perspective only near the distant limb. Sunlight grazes from upper right, quiet nightward falloff on the left. Very thin pale blue atmospheric edge, not a thick neon stripe. Space documentary realism, subtle cinematic exposure, restrained high contrast, no land map stretching, no huge continents, no polar snow cap, no cartoon texture, no illustration or painterly brushstrokes. No spaceship, no rocket, no space station, no stars, no galaxies, no sun disk, no lens flare, no rings, no text, no numbers, no logos, no watermark. Preserve fine cloud microdetail and a smooth convincing planetary curvature. The output is a cutout Earth horizon asset to composite behind a golden anniversary number, not a finished poster.

2026-10-19 update: Passing planets and rings have been removed from the active opening. `gas-giant-albedo-v1.png` is retained as a previously generated asset and is no longer loaded by the scene. The final Earth orbital matte remains active.
